paragraphs: Paul reads Abraham’s faith as a promise with the nations already inside it: Christ, made a curse on the tree, carries the blessing to them, and what arrives is the promise of the Spirit. The psalm sings the same arrival. The Lord is gracious and full of compassion, he feeds those who fear him, he remembers his covenant for ever, and he gives his people the heritage of the nations. These are the goods of the house.

The Gospel shows whose house it is. A strong man keeps his palace at peace until a stronger one takes the armor he trusted; Jesus does it by the finger of God, the Spirit promised to Abraham’s children. Augustine, preaching on this exorcism, says that “{{quote}}” But casting out is only half. A swept and garnished house, left empty, ends worse than it began.

So occupy it. Say the psalm’s refrain in the morning, remembering the covenant. Set a table for someone, since you were fed. Settle one quarrel today, because whoever does not gather, scatters. Better to be occupied by the promise than merely tidy.

quote.text: the prince of this world, who works in the children of disobedience by no other power than the fellowship and the bond of sin, is cast out by our faith.
quote.attribution: St Augustine, Sermon 21 on the New Testament Lessons (Ben. 71), on Matthew 12, the parallel to Luke 11:15–26, §19
quote.translation: Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers, series 1, vol. 6 (ed. P. Schaff)
